title: Data Science
text:
Project Notebooks

Simple TF-IDF Movie Recommender
Link to Google Colab Notebook
This is an exercise from Section 2 of Udemy’s Machine Learning: Natural Language Processing in Python by the Lazy Programmer. The exercise builds a movie recommender with ONLY TF-IDF (no learning).


Time Series Analysis of Movie Sales in Shanghai
Link to Google Colab Notebook
I analyze movie sales in Shanghai from 2012-2015 with exponential smoothing (from statsmodels) and Facebook’s Prophet. The data is reduced from the one used in my research paper “The impact of air pollution on movie theater admissions”.

Welcome to my homepage!
I am an assistant professor of economics at the University of Nebraska at Omaha. My research focuses on applied microeconomics, with particular interests in conflict theory and the Chinese economy. I am also interested in behavioral economics and machine learning/AI, and I enjoy involving students in research projects.
Before returning to UNO, I worked in industry and government as a senior data scientist at Zeenk, a statistical analyst at the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services, and a quantitative analyst at Farm Credit Services of America. Earlier in my academic career, I held full-time faculty positions at Colgate University, Sam Houston State University, and UNO. I earned my Ph.D. in Economics from Kansas State University in 2012.
In my free time, I enjoy reading and playing music.
